bug_semantics: An authenticated BASIC app user can POST /api/attachments/:datasourceId/url because the route uses TABLE/WRITE authorization, which BASIC holds by default. getSignedUploadURL then loads the named S3 datasource's stored IAM credentials and signs PutObject for the request body's bucket and key. Normal S3 datasource configuration does not define a datasource-level bucket, so a BASIC user can obtain a presigned upload URL for any bucket writable by those credentials.
flaw_origin: Commit 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 is the smallest causal BIC: it changes only the relevant route authorization from authorized(BUILDER) to authorized(PermissionType.TABLE, PermissionLevel.READ), exposing the pre-existing caller-controlled S3 signing sink to app users. Its direct parent d180697c7d5ed9c744e2508694b29c3a94c771eb retains BUILDER. Follow-up 9d198b1b00acf8c4ef702f2ebe7758cf0485eead adds the BASIC-user HTTP-200 test, and 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 changes READ to WRITE without removing BASIC access; neither is the first vulnerable change.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 shows author and committer Conor Webb <conorwebb59@gmail.com>, parent d180697c7d5ed9c744e2508694b29c3a94c771eb, the message 'allow app users to generate S3 upload signed URLs', and no AI attribution trailer or bot identity
evidence: The assigned fix_sha disagreement was primary=null versus reviewer=3c235f3456dcfcaf58675f86249060731beec346. The first-party advisory GHSA-xcx6-4f2g-hhgx defines the flaw as BASIC-user route access plus an unpinned caller bucket, and its remediation requires restoring authorized(BUILDER), adding paramResource('datasourceId'), and pinning the bucket to datasource.config.bucket while ignoring the caller-supplied value.

git show --patch 3c235f3456dcfcaf58675f86249060731beec346 shows only a conditional guard: const datasourceBucket = datasource?.config?.bucket; rejection occurs only when datasourceBucket is truthy and differs from the request bucket. The same commit deliberately retains the BASIC-user success test. Its commit object has parent 72e2242de02d3c03543a9be5285337b6334ee8ca and subject 'Fix relationship field name validation'; the full stat touches five files across unrelated relationship-field and linked-row work, so it is an aggregate rather than a dedicated complete security fix.

At tag 3.40.0 (661fe55d609404d073eea86702e0bde7942c3f10), git grep shows TABLE/WRITE on the route, the same conditional datasourceBucket guard, and a BASIC-user test that creates an S3 datasource with accessKeyId and secretAccessKey but no config.bucket, submits bucket 'foo', and expects HTTP 200 plus a signed URL. packages/server/src/integrations/s3.ts defines no bucket field in its datasource schema; bucket exists only as a per-query field. Thus ordinary unconstrained S3 datasources bypass 3c235f3 and retain the advisory's arbitrary-bucket path.

git log --all -S 'bucket must match the datasource configuration' identifies only 3c235f3456dcfcaf58675f86249060731beec346. git log --all -G 'authorized\((BUILDER|PermissionType.TABLE)' on static.ts finds the BIC and the READ-to-WRITE follow-up but no post-BIC restoration of BUILDER. git log --all -G 'paramResource.*datasourceId' on static.ts returns no commit. origin/master c88dcde0cd83040564b5ae14450d8e53a9b4c320 and release v3.44.0-cloud 04f482376f7a5b7a2aa525d4d968549db9f87bd1 still expose the route with TABLE/WRITE; origin/master still has the conditional guard and an S3 datasource schema with no bucket field.

Version-boundary checks resolve 3.39.3 to 7ebb02e6ab8d37f4171e0721090dada62771f57f and 3.39.4 to 54b592e50af8cde47a815e6fe458e24be66a1c3a: the former predates the BIC and retains BUILDER, while the latter contains the BIC and TABLE/WRITE. Although 3c235f3 first appears between 3.39.7 (72e2242de02d3c03543a9be5285337b6334ee8ca) and 3.39.8 (e14ff6788720b986fe52f9f532385717d65759b0), neither 3.39.8 nor the advisory-claimed 3.40.0 boundary is a complete fix boundary.

git diff d180697c7d5ed9c744e2508694b29c3a94c771eb 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 -- packages/server/src/api/routes/static.ts directly proves the relaxed authorization absent in the immediate parent. git cat-file -p on the BIC provides the only attribution evidence used and contains no AI marker.
reasoning: The primary's null fix claim wins and the reviewer's 3c235f3456dcfcaf58675f86249060731beec346 fix claim is wrong. That commit mitigates only nonempty, nonstandard datasource.config.bucket configurations; it neither restores the intended builder boundary nor adds datasource ownership enforcement, and its truthy conditional leaves the normal schema-supported no-bucket configuration fully caller-controlled. The repository's own 3.40.0 BASIC-user regression test exercises exactly that bypass and expects a signed URL. No later reachable commit supplies the missing authorization, ownership, or unconditional bucket pinning, so both fix fields must remain null under the protocol's explicit unpatched exception. The BIC and its direct parent are independently verified, and the BIC commit object contains no AI evidence, making NOT_AI gate-complete despite the unresolved upstream patch state.
remaining_gap: Public history is still unpatched through origin/master c88dcde0cd83040564b5ae14450d8e53a9b4c320 and tagged release v3.44.0-cloud 04f482376f7a5b7a2aa525d4d968549db9f87bd1. No truthful fix_sha or direct_fix_sha can be assigned; the advisory's claimed patched version 3.40.0 is contradicted by its route, S3 schema, controller guard, and BASIC-user HTTP-200 regression test.
